doc.title: Mandel Johnny — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Sinatra, Shirley Horn and film songs
title: Alex North and sensual writing
summary: Mandel names Alex North and David Raksin as sensual writers and praises North's film scores, including Streetcar.

story.theme_name: Playing with and around Miles Davis

blocks.x: Yeah. There aren’t many who can write that sensually, one of the great sensual writers was Alex North, in some of his film scores. David Raksin could do it, probably still can, he’s just joined the board of ASCAP [American Society of Composers, Authors and Publishers] and boy are we glad to have him.
I remember in the early 50s Miles said in print that he was raving about Alex North his, Streetcar Named Desire score he said that was something everybody should hear.

Yeah, most people didn't really realize how great Alex North was, you listen to Cleopatra, Whose Afraid of Virginia Woolf or Spartacus or any one of them they’re just, they are masterpieces. And his orchestration is all like fine line drawing, he really knew his orchestra to.
He used Benny Carter on Streetcar didn’t he?
I think the solo alto saxophone, I think Benny was the…
He certainly was hip enough to do that.
I’ll ask Benny, unless you probably know that to be a fact.
It never occurred to me who it might have been.
I remember reading it, somewhere, I forget where but I think Benny was the solo alto player.
